subject: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail
messages:
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail

Hi Jonas,

We noticed a 41-minute period on 2026-09-30 where our storefront API calls returned 504/timeout behavior and elevated latency right at your scheduled maintenance window (09:30–10:00 PDT). Our billing/procurement team is requesting an SLA credit for that period.

However, our ops team also saw alerts from our CDN provider (FastEdge) that coincided with the same window — they reported a regional control-plane degradation and route flapping for about 20 minutes.

Can you confirm how Redwood attributes that 41-minute degradation for SLA calculations when:
- it overlaps a scheduled maint window we were notified of the day prior, and
- a third-party CDN reported a partial outage at roughly the same time?

We're attaching our edge error log excerpt. Procurement asked for a clear breakdown (start/stop timestamps, whether time inside the maintenance window is excluded, and the reasoning if only a portion is credited).

Thanks,
Jane Liu
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Retail

Attachments: edge_logs_20260930.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads-up and the log extract. I'm looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Rishi (Incident owner) so we can give you a precise timeline and the credit calculation.

Quick notes for context: we did have a scheduled maintenance window for a minor kernel parameter tweak in the US-west control plane from 09:30–10:00 PDT; we published the notice on 2026-09-29. Per the SLA, scheduled maintenance windows are generally exempt from uptime calculations when the customer has been notified. That said, behavior that is attributable to our infrastructure vs. an external provider needs to be separated — we'll attach our internal timing.

Rishi, can you pull the service-side ingress/egress metrics and confirm the period of elevated token-level latency and any retries that might have affected Acme's route? Marissa, once Rishi confirms, can you draft the formal credit calculation and the language for procurement?

Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

> On 2026-09-30 at 09:12, Jane Liu wrote:
> > We noticed a 41-minute period on 2026-09-30 where our storefront API calls returned 504/timeout behavior and elevated latency right at your scheduled maintenance window (09:30–10:00 PDT).

Attachments: scheduled_maintenance_notice_20260930.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail

Hi all,

I've pulled the traces and control-plane logs. Summary:
- 09:28:12 PDT: pre-cutover warmup initiated from control plane.
- 09:30:00 PDT: maintenance state entered (config applied across US-west cluster).
- 09:30:00–09:34:40 PDT: we saw an increase in tail latency for some instances (retries visible in request logs).
- 09:34:40–09:54:00 PDT: a subset of customer requests experienced 504s. This period overlaps with reported FastEdge partial outage (their incident #FE-9081 indicates regional route flapping 09:33–09:53 PDT).
- 09:54:01 PDT: request success rates returned to baseline.

Notes on attribution: the first ~4.5 minutes (09:30–09:34:40) show internal traces consistent with KV cache warming and transient connection churn on our side; those are squarely within our maintenance action. The longer window of 09:34:40–09:54:00 includes strong evidence of external CDN route failures — FastEdge's BGP convergence events correlate with spikes in origin retries and 504s.

Operationally we separate the timeline into:
1) 09:30:00–09:34:40: internal maintenance impact (21% of the 41-minute observed degradation)
2) 09:34:40–09:54:00: mixed-origin where both our retries and FastEdge route instability amplified errors (79% of the remaining period)

I'll attach the raw ingress summary and per-pod error counts. From an SLA calculation perspective: because Acme was notified of the maintenance, the time strictly resulting from our scheduled maintenance is eligible for exclusion from uptime (per Section 4.2 of the SLA). For the mixed-origin portion, our policy treats incidents where an external provider causes the majority of error amplification as non-Redwood-attributable, but we do a proportional apportionment when root cause is mixed.

I'll hand this to Marissa for the precise credit math and the wording for procurement.

Rishi
Sr. Incident Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ingress_summary_20260930.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeretail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail

Hi Jane — thanks for the patience. Based on Rishi's timeline and our SLA terms, here's the proposed calculation and next steps:

1) Total observed customer impact window: 09:13–09:54 PDT per your edge logs (we verified 504s/latency spikes focused 09:30:00–09:54:00). We align to 09:30–09:54 as the relevant service-affecting interval.
2) Exclusion for scheduled maintenance: Section 4.2 allows exclusion of the portion directly caused by Redwood maintenance when the customer was notified. Rishi's traces indicate 09:30:00–09:34:40 (4 minutes, 40 seconds) attributable primarily to our maintenance.
3) Mixed-origin period (09:34:40–09:54:00 = 19 minutes, 20 seconds): per our remediation policy we apportion credit where an external provider predominantly caused amplification. FastEdge's incident report shows route instability for ~20 minutes overlapping this interval; we propose attributing 80% of the mixed-origin period to FastEdge and 20% to Redwood's retries/handling.

Credit math (simple uptime minutes excluded vs. total SLA window):
- Total potential SLA impact minutes in the billing day: 24*60 (we'll apply the standard monthly credit computation for the billing cycle). For this discrete request, we propose Redwood-eligible exclusion: 4.67 minutes (maintenance) + 3.85 minutes (20% of the 19.33 mixed minutes) = 8.52 minutes.

Marissa's proposed action: we will issue a one-time pro-rata credit equivalent to 8.52 minutes of downtime for the relevant billing month. If Acme prefers a conservative full-window credit (41 minutes) for customer experience reasons, we can escalate for an exceptions panel review.

Please confirm whether Acme accepts the proportional credit or wishes to escalate. Once accepted, procurement and billing will process the credit against invoice INV-ACME-202609.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment references: ingress_summary_20260930.csv, sla_excerpt_v2.pdf

From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com, CDN Ops <ops@fastedge.io>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service window attribution — request for SLA credit and calculation detail

Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown and the arithmetic. Acme appreciates the proportional approach and Rishi's detailed timeline. Procurement has reviewed the numbers; we accept the pro-rata credit of 8.52 minutes to be applied against INV-ACME-202609.

Small ask: could Redwood include the following in the credit memo for our finance team — the breakdown of minutes and the statement that FastEdge's incident contributed ~80% of the mixed-origin period (we'll accept their incident id FE-9081 as corroboration)? Also please loop in billing so we can close the invoice.

If Redwood would like the exceptions panel to review for goodwill, we are open but not necessary.

Thanks,
Jane Liu
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Retail
